editorial:
Imagine living on a massive farm in Iowa where your father holds all the power and keeps everyone on a short leash. You get to see three sisters who have spent their whole lives trying to please a man who is nearly impossible to satisfy. The vibe here is heavy and tense, focusing on family secrets and the kind of anger that builds up over decades. It feels like a modern take on a classic tragedy, where the land they live on is just as important as the people fighting over it. You will feel for the daughters as they realize their father might not be the man they thought he was.

The acting is the best part of the whole experience, especially the way the sisters interact. While the story moves a bit slowly at times, the emotional payoff is huge. It is a great pick if you enjoy deep dramas about broken families. If you want to see it, you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or you might want to add the Blu-ray to your physical collection if you like collecting older gems. Just make sure you have some tissues ready because it gets pretty sad.
endingExplained: You find out that the father was actually abusive to his daughters when they were young. In the end, the sisters finally face the truth about their childhood trauma. They realize that the land was used as a tool to control them. They eventually break free from their father's shadow, letting go of the hate and the farm to start their own lives with a clean slate.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas with deep secrets.
